# Supply Risk Monitoring Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Supply Risk Monitoring Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded supplier files, proposed ERP, risk-feed, Power BI and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for supplier, risk-feed, reporting and collaboration connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare procurement, supply chain and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview without publishing. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Risk-rule ownership | Have the business owner approve the composite-health weighting and risk-tier rules coded in the portable agent before scoring real suppliers. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** How supplier evidence is assembled for continuity review across ERP, supplier-management, logistics, quality and external-risk sources. Agree where fragmented analysis delays continuity planning before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Supplier | Category | Evidence sources consulted | Open incidents | Backup options on record | Review requested | Review completed | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Procurement business owner | Approve supplier-risk scope, scoring rules, escalation and success measures; keep synthetic figures out of customer results. |
| Authorized procurement owners | Decide any outreach, qualification, selection, allocation, contracting or ordering through approved procurement and supplier-management tools. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any supplier connection is approved. |
| Supplier data and connection owners | Approve ERP, risk-feed, Power BI and Teams access; record dedicated connection references and least-privilege identities. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check SR-01 through SR-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject truncated, reasoning-only or wrong-agent evidence. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route procurement decisions to authorized owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for supplier-risk review are agreed.
- [ ] The business owner records how supplier evidence is assembled today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/supplier-risk-monitoring/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated procurement audience and least-privilege scopes for supplier and spend data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/supplier-risk-monitoring/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/supplier-risk-monitoring/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/supplier-risk-monitoring/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/supplier-risk-monitoring/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Supply Risk Monitoring Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_supplier-risk-monitoring-review-rules.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_supplier-risk-monitoring-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_alternative_sourcing
9. Add skill: aibast_disruption_alerts
10. Add skill: aibast_risk_dashboard
11. Add skill: aibast_supplier_scorecard
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass SR-01: Supply Chain Director
15. Pass SR-02: Procurement Manager
16. Pass SR-03: Supply Chain Director
17. Pass SR-04: Procurement Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: SR-01, SR-02, SR-03, SR-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `SupplierRiskMonitoringAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged SR-01 through SR-04 prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final response; reasoning traces and truncated frames are not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing supplier, spend or incident data. Request only the read scopes the approved supplier and risk sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management — read:** Bind approved read-only finance and operations connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not qualify, select or reallocate; compare options for review and state that no supplier was contacted. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the absent evidence; do not browse, invent or substitute another record.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved external risk feeds

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved external risk feeds — read:** Wrap each approved feed in a custom connector exposing read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved external risk feeds:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved external risk feeds:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved external risk feeds:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not disqualify; present the incident as synthetic evidence that needs validation. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report the absent evidence; do not browse, invent or substitute another record.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Power BI

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

1. **Bind Power BI — read:** Query an approved curated dataset read-only with the Power BI connector.

2. **Identity for Power BI:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Power BI:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Power BI:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not browse or change records; use only the fixed synthetic snapshot. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, message or supplier action succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Gate any posting workflow behind procurement approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Contact no supplier; show the synthetic evidence and name the authorized procurement route. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return review options and name the authorized procurement owner; perform no action.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Procurement workflow and contract systems

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

1. **Bind Procurement workflow and contract systems — write:** Keep unavailable until an approval workflow and explicit procurement tools pass review (preview).

2. **Identity for Procurement workflow and contract systems:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Procurement workflow and contract systems:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Procurement workflow and contract systems:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not qualify, select or reallocate; compare options for review and state that no supplier was contacted. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return review options and name the authorized procurement owner; perform no action.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supplier data and connection owners

Create read tools with dedicated connection references for approved ERP, supplier, quality, financial, logistics, external-risk and reporting data.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved supplier, risk, reporting and collaboration connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] No lookup, message or supplier action is claimed unless an approved production tool returns evidence of success.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as procurement users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, tiers and premiums are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked supplier-risk corpus | All four cases, SR-01 through SR-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Procurement authority | Any supplier contact, qualification, selection, allocation, contract, order or sourcing approval is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Production publication has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved procurement audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review supplier-risk sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
